messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Renewals <renewals@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly Sync: Roadmap Exceptions Playbook — owners & QBR inputs

Hi all,

Thanks for carving time in the weekly cross-functional sync today. I want to lock down owners and deliverables ahead of the QBR so we can avoid last-minute exceptions during exec review. High level: we have three outstanding roadmap exceptions that could affect the QBR narrative (latency SLO on Embed-Prod, Dedicated rollout lag in eu-west, and billing terms for reserved capacity).

Action asks (please reply with owner + ETA):
- Confirm remediation approach for Embed-Prod latency regression (SRE + Runtime) — owner? ETA?
- Decide canary cadence vs. immediate rollback for the Dedicated eu-west rollout — owner and fallback policy
- Approve contract language for Reserved Capacity credits (legal/sales input) — who will send redlines to Acme?

I've attached a short 'playbook' PDF with proposed step sequences for each exception and a QBR-prep checklist (spreadsheet). Jordan, adding you to keep Acme aligned on timelines; if any of the exceptions change the delivery/commit, flag here.

Please respond with explicit owners by EOD Wednesday (05/05). If you prefer to triage in today's sync and I'll capture notes, say so.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Partnerships (Acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: roadmap-exceptions-playbook.pdf (summary, 6 pages), QBR-prep-checklist.xlsx (sheet: owners)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly Sync: Roadmap Exceptions Playbook — owners & QBR inputs

Kimberly — quick take after reviewing the playbook. I'll take primary for Embed-Prod latency (SRE + Runtime coordination). Plan:
- Immediate: enable conservative batching cap to reduce tail variance (today)
- 48h: run targeted perf profile and validate kernel selection heuristics (runtime)
- 5 business days: deploy hotfix canary + monitor 1p traces and token latency.

ETA for owner-closed doc: 2027-05-10. I'll post the perf snapshot to the Drive link.

One ask for Marissa/Vivek: if we flip batching caps it may increase token cost for high-concurrency routes — need short cost delta for QBR. Can someone post a condensed cost delta row in the QBR checklist?

—Rishi
SRE Lead

Thanks Kimberly and team — appreciated the clear plan. Quick responses:
- Acme can tolerate a short canary for Hosted embed stability; please share monitoring thresholds you want us to watch (error rate, p95 token latency).
- For reserved capacity credits: Jordan confirms Acme legal is open to a compromise where credits are tied to documented SLA misses rather than blanket percentage. I'll await Marissa's redlines.
- On the EU Dedicated rollout: Acme would prefer a phased go-live with a backstop region in us-west for critical traffic — I'll include expected traffic % in a follow-up note (by EOD Monday).

Jordan Mills
Director, Platform Partnerships
Acme Corp
